jobs.title: AI Architect
Embedded Controls Software Engineer
jobs.description:
Embedded Controls Software Engineer

At DeWarmte, we develop technology that helps homes move away from gas. Our heat pumps combine hardware, embedded control software, cloud services and data – and the quality of the software connecting those elements directly determines how well our products perform in customers’ homes.


We are looking for an experienced Embedded Controls Software Engineer to develop and evolve the software that operates our heat pumps and, increasingly, a broader range of connected energy devices. As part of our Control & Data team, you will work directly on production software, refine control algorithms, improve product performance and help shape the next generation of our embedded software platform.


This is a hands-on engineering role at the intersection of software, hardware, control engineering and energy systems. You will work on technology that is already operating in customers’ homes while building the technical foundations for future products and use cases.

Your mission

Build reliable, efficient and extensible control software that enables our products to operate intelligently in an increasingly connected and flexible energy system.
You will inherit working software already deployed in the field. Your job is to understand it deeply, maintain and improve it, and progressively evolve its architecture to support new products, control strategies and regulatory requirements.
Together with the Lead Controls & Data Engineer and our Hardware R&D team, you will help build an embedded software platform that can scale with DeWarmte’s ambitions.

What you will do

Maintain and improve our control software

  • Work directly in the production code that controls our heat pumps.

  • Design, build, test and deploy new control functionality.

  • Develop, refine and validate control algorithms to improve product performance, stability, safety, energy efficiency and customer comfort.

  • Use operational data and real-world measurements to understand product behaviour and identify opportunities for improvement.

  • Diagnose complex behaviour across software, electronics, sensors, hydraulics and the physical installation.

  • Improve automated testing, simulation, observability and release practices.

  • Help ensure reliable operation of both newly developed products and our existing installed fleet.

Evolve our embedded software platform

  • Contribute to the architecture and technical evolution of our on-device software stack.

  • Gradually migrate our existing Python-based control software to a compiled systems programming language, with Rust as the preferred direction.

  • Improve software maintainability, runtime reliability, resource efficiency and testability while preserving proven control behaviour.

  • Develop and extend our over-the-air (OTA) software update mechanisms, enabling reliable and controlled software deployments across our connected device fleet.

  • Contribute to the development of our next-generation embedded hardware configuration, working closely with our Hardware R&D colleagues on hardware-software integration and platform design.

  • Establish clear interfaces and reusable software components that allow the platform to evolve without unnecessary complexity.

Expand our control capabilities

  • Extend our control software to support new devices, product configurations and energy management use cases.

  • Develop control strategies that respond to external signals, dynamic energy prices, grid constraints and demand-side flexibility opportunities.

  • Translate evolving regulatory requirements and interoperability standards into robust, testable software functionality.

  • Develop interfaces that enable our products to interact with external energy management systems, other connected devices and third-party services.

  • Help balance energy efficiency, customer comfort, equipment longevity and flexibility in our control strategies.

Work across the product

You will collaborate closely with colleagues in hardware, software, data, product development, assembly, installation and service. You will help resolve immediate customer and operational issues while protecting the long-term quality of our software platform.

You will actively contribute to technical discussions, code reviews, documentation and shared engineering practices, ensuring that our software can be understood, maintained and evolved by the entire team.

What success looks like in your first month

  • You develop a solid understanding of our existing heat pump control software, development workflows and embedded environment.

  • You become familiar with the physical behaviour of our products and the interfaces between software and hardware.

  • You actively contribute to day-to-day software development, debugging and maintenance.

  • By the end of your first month, you are able to independently drive the development of new control functionality, with support from the wider team where needed.

In the following months

  • You take increasing technical ownership of our on-device control software.

  • You independently design, implement, test and deploy improvements to our control algorithms and functionality.

  • You contribute to measurable improvements in product reliability, performance and software quality.

  • You help define and validate the architecture for migrating our Python-based control software to a compiled language.

  • You begin extending and improving our OTA software update mechanisms.

As the role develops

  • You drive the progressive migration of our control software towards a modern, robust and maintainable systems programming stack.

  • New control functionality can be delivered predictably and safely across our installed fleet.

  • You contribute to the design, development and validation of our next-generation embedded hardware and software platform.

  • Our control software supports an increasingly diverse range of devices, regulatory requirements, interoperability standards and energy management use cases.

  • Critical software components are well documented, thoroughly tested and understood by more than one engineer.

  • You become a key technical contributor to the evolution of DeWarmte’s control software platform.

What we are looking for

Essential experiences and skills

  • Several years of hands-on software engineering experience, ideally at mid- to senior level, including experience with production systems.

  • Practical experience developing, implementing and validating control algorithms for physical products, machines or energy systems.

  • Practical experience with HVAC systems, thermal energy systems or controllable energy assets in the context of demand-side flexibility, including an understanding of their physical behaviour and operational constraints.

  • Experience developing software in embedded or hardware-connected environments.

  • Hands-on experience with a modern systems programming language such as Rust or Go. Extensive experience with C, C++ or comparable low-level languages is also relevant, provided you are willing and able to transition to a modern systems programming stack.

  • A good working knowledge of Python and the ability to understand, maintain and evolve an existing Python codebase.

  • Strong engineering fundamentals, including version control, automated testing, code reviews and CI/CD workflows.

  • The ability to reason across software, hardware and physical-system behaviour and systematically diagnose complex problems.

  • Comfort working with modern LLM-based and agentic software development tools and workflows, while maintaining a high standard of engineering quality, code review and verification.

  • The ability to take functionality through the complete development lifecycle, from design and implementation to testing, deployment and real-world operation.

Additional valuable experience

  • Embedded Linux development, particularly experience with Yocto or Buildroot, custom system images and embedded Linux deployment workflows.

  • Direct experience developing control software or control algorithms for heat pumps.

  • Experience with OTA software updates, connected-device fleet management and reliable software deployment to remotely operated devices.

  • Familiarity with industrial or energy-sector communication protocols, interoperability standards and regulatory requirements.

  • Experience with simulation, hardware-in-the-loop testing, control system modelling or optimisation.

  • Experience with front-end paradigms and languages, whether web-based or native, preferably using modern JavaScript or TypeScript frameworks.

We do not expect you to bring experience in every one of these areas. We value strong software and control engineering fundamentals, intellectual curiosity and the ability to quickly develop a deep understanding of complex physical products.

How you work

  • You take ownership of problems from initial investigation through to implementation, validation and deployment.

  • You enjoy working at the intersection of software and the physical world and are interested in understanding why a system behaves the way it does.

  • You solve urgent problems without allowing permanent workarounds to become the architecture.

  • You balance pragmatic improvements today with the technical investments needed to scale tomorrow.

  • You use modern development tools, including AI-assisted and agentic workflows, to work effectively without compromising reliability or your understanding of the software.

  • You explain complex technical matters clearly to people with different backgrounds.

  • You share knowledge by default and build software that other engineers can intuitively understand, easily test and safely change.

  • You are comfortable switching between debugging a specific installation, refining a control algorithm and developing the architecture for our next generation of products.

What you will get

  • Direct influence on technology that contributes to the energy transition.

  • Ownership of software that sits at the heart of a real physical product.

  • The opportunity to work on challenging problems at the intersection of embedded software, control engineering and energy systems.

  • The opportunity to shape the transition towards a modern embedded software platform

  • A role that starts deeply hands-on and grows into broader technical ownership and architectural responsibility.

  • Close collaboration with colleagues across the complete product lifecycle.

What we offer

  • A monthly gross salary between €4.500 and €6.000, based on full-time.

  • 27 vacation days plus 8% holiday allowance.

  • Participation in our SAR (Stock Appreciation Rights) programme.

  • Plenty of ownership and responsibility from day one.

  • The opportunity to shape products that directly contribute to the energy transition.

  • A talented, ambitious, and highly collaborative team.

  • A healthy daily lunch at the office.

  • Laptop and everything you need to do your best work.

  • Regular team events, company drinks, our annual beach day, and winter trip.

  • Lots of room to grow, develop yourself, and make a lasting impact.

Interested?

Do you want to build intelligent control software for real physical products and help shape the next generation of connected, energy-efficient heating and energy systems?

We would like to meet you!

Compensation: €4.5K – €6K per month

  • • €4.5K – €6K per month

jobs.title: Vice President of Engineering
jobs.description:
Vice President of Engineering

About Andercore

Andercore is the AI-native supplier of industrial materials and goods for energy and infrastructure. We execute trade and distribution end-to-end, on our own account, at the speed of compute - and we are becoming the supplier of record for the entire industry.

Industrial procurement is a €900B market in Europe alone and the largest manual market on earth. 95% of customers have no direct access to global supply chains. Materials pass through four or five intermediaries before they reach a site, and 40% of the margin evaporates on the way. For decades, the operating system of this industry was people: people to source, negotiate, finance, ship, and sell.

We built the alternative from scratch. We are the supplier. We buy from global sources and sell to European customers on our own account. Our AI runs the full trade: sourcing, quality, pricing, sales, logistics, credit, and financing. One request. A firm quote in minutes. Delivered on time. For the customer, it feels like buying from their preferred local supplier. No warehouses. No fleet. No inventory risk. Every trade is pre-sold before it is bought.

We are also the credit counterparty. Customers are scored and insured in minutes and get up to 60 days of payment terms priced into the quote itself. The working capital behind every trade is bank-funded, not equity-funded.

Where we are today:

  • Strong triple-digit-million euro turnover run rate, the majority of it from repeat customers

  • Seven European markets live, sourced from suppliers across Asia and beyond

  • 80+ people across Berlin (HQ), London, and Shanghai

  • $90M raised in equity and debt, including our $40M Series B, from Atomico, Project A, Target Global, and Inven Capital - with working capital facilities from UniCredit and KfW

The margin is in the bits. The moat is in the atoms. We are building the supplier of record for industrial materials - and redefining how global trade works in one of the largest and most essential industries on earth.

Role Overview

As VP Engineering, you own the Engineering organization and turn our platform and AI vision into shipped systems. You report to the Chief Product Officer and partner closely with product, commercial, operations, and finance. You lead our Senior Product Engineers, Staff Engineers and QA, and work closely with our product managers, who own product and design.

This is an execution mandate. You carve our core systems into a modern platform, build our AI agents into one holistic system that runs the trade lifecycle end-to-end, and scale the teams that deliver it. You inherit a working machine at full speed: your job is to rebuild it in flight without losing a day of momentum. In your first year, the priorities are the carve-out of our transaction core and bringing our AI agents into one orchestrating layer.

Key Responsibilities

AI and Automation

  • Build our AI agents into one holistic, orchestrating AI layer across sourcing, pricing, quoting, sales, logistics, and financing.

  • Drive automation of the full transaction lifecycle, and own automation-rate and no touch-quote targets as first-class delivery KPIs.

  • Work with our data team, which sits with the CPO, on systems that make our trade flows a compounding advantage, so every transaction makes the system smarter.

  • Keep us at the practical frontier of agentic AI: ship what creates leverage now, skip what is demo-ware.

  • Put the guardrails, evals, and human-in-the loop controls in place so automation stays reliable where it matters most: money touching and customer-facing paths, where a wrong output is a real loss, not just a bug.

Platform and Architecture

  • Own execution of the target architecture for the Andercore platform, the system of record for industrial trade.

  • Lead the carve-out of our transaction core into a modern, modular light ERP (a lean core system for our trade transactions), with a clear migration path and zero disruption to daily trading.

  • Shape the role of Salesforce in our landscape: decide what stays on the platform, what moves to the new core, and how the two work together.

  • Make pragmatic build-vs-buy calls within the platform strategy and keep technology cost per transaction on a falling curve.

  • Make new-market launch a repeatable platform motion: multiple geographies, currencies, languages, and compliance regimes, built in rather than bolted on.

  • Keep the platform ready to pass technical due diligence at any moment: architecture, data, and security in shape for the next financing round.

Engineering Organization and Talent

  • Lead the Engineering organization: onsite talent in Berlin and a nearshoring team. Team structure and ways of working stay in-house, and you manage the nearshoring team directly and actively, not at arm's length through a vendor.

  • Build lean by default. The goal is not to grow headcount but to build a small, high-leverage team and raise output through AI across the engineering workflow. You lead as an AI-first engineering leader.

  • Hire and develop senior engineering leaders, including 1–2 Staff Engineers who report to you and own architecture across teams, and raise the talent bar with every hire.

  • Build an engineering culture of ownership, speed, and craftsmanship: small teams, high leverage, no bureaucracy.

  • Stay hands-on: review designs with your Staff Engineers, pair on the hardest problems, unblock teams, and keep decisions close to the code.

Enablement and Data Integrity

  • Enable business teams to build and automate with AI safely. Set the paved paths, standards, and review practices that let non-engineers move fast without compromising quality, security, or the systems underneath.

  • Partner with the CPO, who owns data, on data integrity: build systems that keep one source of truth with clear access and quality controls, so that faster building never degrades the data the company runs on.

  • Make speed and safety one operating model, not a trade-off, and communicate it across the company so every team knows how to move quickly within clear boundaries.

Delivery and Cross-Functional Partnership

  • Act as technical sparring partner to the CPO on architecture, roadmap feasibility, and sequencing.

  • Translate the product roadmap into shipped software, and turn front-line needs from commercial and operations into delivery.

  • Support the CPO and CEO in technical due diligence with a clear, numbers-backed view of architecture, data, and AI.

  • Communicate technical priorities and trade-offs transparently across the company, so everyone understands what we build and why.

What Success Looks Like

  • Engineering operates with clear ownership and no loss of delivery speed.

  • Our transaction core runs on a modern, modular platform: the carve-out is live and the migration path is executed.

  • One orchestrating AI system increases automation rate and transactions per employee, quarter over quarter.

  • Technology cost per transaction falls while volume grows.

  • Architecture, systems, and AI stand up to any technical due diligence.

  • Hiring runs fast and consistently: senior hires close within six weeks, with one bar across interviewers.

What You Bring

  • Senior engineering leadership at scale, having run and grown multi-team organizations, ideally across more than one location.

  • Deep experience with transactional platforms, ERP-style systems, or comparable systems of record, ideally including regulated financial flows such as payments, lending, or KYC, and re-platforming or carve-outs in a live environment.

  • Hands-on track record shipping AI or ML in production, with a real sense for where agentic AI creates leverage today.

  • A demonstrated AI-first, lean mindset: you have applied AI in your own engineering organization to raise output without growing headcount, not just talked about it.

  • Strong architectural judgment, with security and data protection built into your decisions, and enough technical depth to stay close to the code.

  • The judgment to know where reliability must be absolute and where speed wins: you move fast on everything reversible and hold a high correctness bar on the irreversible, money-touching paths.

  • A plus: a track record of enabling non-engineering teams to build safely with AI, balancing speed

  • against quality and data integrity, and the communication skills to carry that across a whole company.

  • A plus: comfort in a company where operations come first and software follows, turning manual services into products.

  • A commercial mindset: you anchor engineering decisions in unit economics, working capital, and speed for buyers and suppliers.

  • A plus: experience with Salesforce as part of a larger system landscape.

Practical details

  • Location: Berlin

  • Process: conversations with the CPO, the CEO, Chief of Staff, and members of the engineering team.

We are an equal-opportunity employer and welcome applicants from all backgrounds, regardless of race, ethnicity, gender identity or expression, sexual orientation, religion, age, disability, or any other characteristic. We believe that diversity drives innovation, creativity, and collective strength.

jobs.title: Senior Financial Systems Engineer (m/f/d)
jobs.description:
Senior Financial Systems Engineer (m/f/d)

We're building a new global Berlitz, and this is your opportunity to help shape it. Nearly 150 years of expertise, meeting the ambition and technology to power a new era of learning.

If you are the kind of person who thrives in a fast-paced environment, isn’t afraid of a blank page, and is excited to help shape the future of a global company undergoing a significant transformation, you might belong at Berlitz!

About the role

Berlitz is rebuilding its commercial and financial platform. That includes a new CRM, usage-based billing, modern payment processing, and a consolidated ERP, all supporting new digital products for learners, teachers, and enterprise customers.

We're looking for a Senior Financial Systems Engineer to own the flow of money through that platform, from quote and checkout through billing and payment to the general ledger. You'll be the technical authority on how our systems exchange financial data. You'll make sure every customer, invoice, payment, refund, and credit reconciles cleanly at month-end.

This is a hands-on engineering role that sits at the intersection of engineering and finance. You'll report into Engineering and work day to day with Finance, RevOps, and our external NetSuite implementation partner.

What you'll do

  • Own the architecture and data contracts for our order-to-cash flow across HubSpot, Stripe, Adyen, Metronome, and NetSuite.

  • Build and maintain integrations using NetSuite SuiteScript and REST/SuiteTalk, PSP APIs and webhooks, and our iPaaS (Workato), choosing custom code or low-code where each makes sense.

  • Design reconciliation between payment processors, billing, bank settlements, and the ledger, and build the jobs, alerts, and audit trails that keep it reliable.

  • Model prepaid credit packages and usage-based consumption correctly, including deferred revenue, drawdown, expiry, refunds, and credit notes.

  • Support multi-entity, multi-currency operations, including subsidiaries, intercompany flows, FX, and tax handling.

  • Act as the technical counterpart to our NetSuite implementation partner: review designs, challenge assumptions, and take ownership of what they build.

  • Partner with Finance to shorten and de-risk month-end close by removing manual work and fixing data quality at the source.

  • Document the financial data model and integrations so the platform is supportable beyond you.

What you'll bring

  • 6+ years in software engineering, with at least 3 years building or owning financial, billing, or payments systems.

  • Hands-on NetSuite development experience (SuiteScript 2.x, REST/SuiteTalk, saved searches) and a solid understanding of its record model, including customers, sales orders, invoices, payments, deposits, and journals.

  • Production experience integrating Stripe and/or Adyen, including webhooks, idempotency, payouts and settlement reports, disputes, and fees.

  • Real accounting literacy. You can explain revenue recognition, deferred revenue, cash application, and bank reconciliation, and you know why they matter to Finance.

  • Strong integration engineering fundamentals: API design, event-driven patterns, retries and error handling, and data validation.

  • Comfort working across teams and translating between engineers, accountants, and commercial stakeholders.

  • Good judgement under deadline pressure, with the ability to ship pragmatically without creating reconciliation debt.

Nice to have

  • Experience with usage-based or consumption billing platforms (Metronome, Orb, Chargebee, or similar).

  • Experience with HubSpot, Salesforce, or other CRM-to-ERP integrations.

  • iPaaS experience (Workato, Boomi, Celigo, MuleSoft).

  • Experience migrating from a legacy billing or CRM system to a new stack.

  • Exposure to SOC 2 / ISO 27001 controls around financial systems.

  • Experience at a multi-country business or in education / subscription services.

What success looks like

  • First 90 days: You understand our current order-to-cash flows end to end. You've taken technical ownership of the payments-to-ledger integration and identified the biggest reconciliation risks.

  • First 6 months: New products bill, collect, and post to NetSuite correctly across entities and currencies. Month-end reconciliation between PSPs and the ledger is largely automated.

  • First year: Our financial systems are well documented, monitored, and trusted by Finance, and they're ready to scale to new products and markets.

Why Berlitz

  • A rare chance to shape a financial platform nearly from scratch at a global brand with a long history.

  • Direct impact on how the company operates and reports, with high visibility across Engineering, Finance, and leadership.

  • A team that values pragmatic engineering and cross-functional ownership.

At Berlitz, connecting people across languages and cultures is at the heart of what we do. Our global workplace reflects the diverse world we serve, bringing together different backgrounds, experiences and perspectives. We create an inclusive environment where everyone has an equal opportunity to belong, contribute and grow.

Ready to shape what’s next? Join us and help build the future with us.

Who We Are

AI is changing how software gets built. Code production is becoming a commodity. The focus is shifting from writing code to specifying, orchestrating, verifying, and governing change – and the toolchain is the new constraint.

We are at the center of this shift. We build Develocity, a toolchain observability and intelligence platform used by some of the world's leading software organizations – Netflix, Airbnb, Spotify, SAP, major global banks, and hundreds more. Develocity helps software teams achieve delivery excellence through deep observability, build and test acceleration, and AI-powered intelligence across the entire toolchain – with support for Gradle Build Tool, Apache Maven™, sbt, npm, Python, and Bazel.

Software Engineer (Fleet) - London

About Us

At Teton, we are redefining the role of healthcare workers through cutting-edge AI technology. Facing a global nursing shortage, our solutions offer vital support to overburdened health systems. With thousands of patient rooms across 4 countries already benefiting from our technology, we are aiming to expand to much more. We distinguish ourselves by focusing relentlessly on product excellence and user experience, rapidly deploying solutions that make a real difference.

The Job

Every patient room we deploy into puts another device on infrastructure we don't control, in a building we can't easily visit, running software that has to keep working. We're looking for an Engineer to own that problem: the systems, tooling, and infrastructure that let us ship to thousands of edge devices confidently and understand what they're doing once they're out there.

In this role, you will focus on the following areas of interest:

  • Fleet Management: Build and run the systems that provision, monitor, and manage our devices in the field, from first boot in a hospital room to end of life.

  • OTA & Release Engineering: Own how software gets onto devices: staged rollouts, health checks, automatic rollback, and the confidence that a bad release won't take down a ward.

  • Observability: Design the telemetry, logging, and alerting that tell us a device is degrading before a nurse notices. Make remote debugging possible so we don't fly to fix things.

  • Device Bring-Up & Debugging: Work with our hardware and firmware teams on new hardware revisions, reproduce field issues on the bench, and get to the bottom of problems that span kernel, driver, network, and application.

  • Infrastructure & Tooling: Build the CI/CD, image builds, and internal tools that let the whole engineering team ship to hardware quickly and safely.

  • Documentation: Maintain clear and detailed documentation of your work to ensure easy collaboration and knowledge sharing within the team.

Qualifications:

  • Solid experience running Linux systems in production: ideally embedded or edge Linux, not just cloud VMs.

  • Proficiency in Rust and/or Javascript/Typescript and/or Python

  • Experience with device fleets at scale: provisioning, OTA update mechanisms (Mender, RAUC, balena, or something you built yourself), and remote access to constrained devices.

  • Familiarity with Linux internals: systemd, kernel modules, device tree, networking stack, containers.

  • Experience with observability tooling (Prometheus, Grafana, OpenTelemetry, or similar) and designing what to measure, not just wiring up dashboards.

  • Comfortable with hardware debugging: serial consoles, working alongside hardware engineers

  • Understanding of communication protocols and how devices talk to each other and to us: I2C, SPI, UART, Bluetooth, Wi-Fi, MQTT.

  • Pragmatism about networks you don't control: restrictive hospital IT, VLANs, proxies, flaky Wi-Fi, and long offline periods.

  • Strong problem-solving skills and the ability to work independently as well as part of a team.

  • Experience with the NVIDIA Jetson platform and Linux for Tegra is a big plus.

  • Experience with Yocto, Debian packaging, or custom image builds is a plus.

  • Experience in the medical device or healthcare technology field is a plus.

What We Offer

  • Participation in our warrant program (stock options).

  • Work with state-of-the-art technology in a pioneering field.

  • A vibrant, learning-focused work environment.

  • A role where you can make a significant impact on healthcare delivery.

Join Our Team

We're looking for individuals who share our vision and value ownership and entrepreneurship over a conventional job. At Teton, you'll have the chance to make a real impact with your work. If you're ready for more than just a job, come aboard and be part of our mission to transform healthcare.

About the Role

We’re looking for a Revenue Operations Manager to build and run the systems behind Tebi’s revenue engine, from how we find and win merchants to how we onboard, retain and grow them across seven European markets.

You’ll apply skills like building enrichment flows, tracking buying signals, setting up outbound and automating workflows in HubSpot and the tools around it across the customer lifecycle, from lead enrichment and outbound to onboarding handover, customer health and expansion. You’ll report to our RevOps Lead and work closely with Sales, Marketing, Onboarding, Account Management and the Data team.

This is a hands-on role where speed matters. You’ll build with Clay, HubSpot, n8n, APIs, webhooks and AI, and take every idea from first experiment to a system the whole go-to-market team relies on. You understand what drives revenue, so you know what is worth building, and you work in short loops: ship fast, measure, learn and adapt quickly.

What You’ll Do

Build the acquisition engine

  • Build enrichment flows, ideal customer profile scoring and lead routing that turn raw leads into clear next actions for reps in HubSpot.

  • Design and automate signal tracking across the funnel, including walk-in activity in emerging markets not yet visible in HubSpot.

  • Build outbound plays and sequencing systems for sales-led and PLG motions, and run experiments to learn how best to reach customers.

  • Prototype and improve an AI outbound assistant that saves reps time, with a human in the loop.

Build the processes and automation behind onboarding, retention and expansion

  • Design and automate the Sales-to-Onboarding handover process across our toolstack, replacing manual steps and setting milestones, ownership and service levels from signed to live, with alerts when a merchant stalls.

  • Set up the retention signals and risk alerts that matter, each routed to a clear action and owner.

  • Design the expansion framework from scratch for sales-led (Account Manager-led) and PLG (automated, in-product or lifecycle) upsell, and build the plays, sequences and automation behind it in our toolstack.

  • Measure and refine these processes against pipeline, retention and expansion outcomes, and talk to reps, Account Managers and merchants about their pain points to turn what you learn into better workflows and systems.

  • Build and maintain the integrations across our toolstack, including HubSpot, BigQuery and the enrichment and outbound tools, and document system logic so it scales with the team.

What You’ll Need

  • Around 3 or more years of relevant experience in RevOps, sales operations or customer success operations, or an equivalent role in B2B SaaS.

  • Hands-on experience building enrichment flows, signal tracking and outbound systems.

  • Experience in high-velocity SaaS or an agency.

jobs.description:
Internship - 3D Graphics for Robotics

Opening

WE CANNOT PROVIDE VISA SPONSORSHIP


Details

About the company

Fiducial is a young but fast-growing deep-tech start-up with big ambitions at the frontier of autonomy, perception, and defence. Our core expertise lies in 3D vision and graphics technologies which we deploy in a dual-use context for inspection and defence. This role will initially focus mainly on the defence context where we are developing software for advanced on-board UAV situational awareness in military applications. Our solutions are aimed to operate with low-cost and widely available sensors and compute. From there, we plan to develop a line-up of interconnected solutions to safeguard European safety.

Our team consists of engineers that are passionate about the technology and solutions they develop. The only time most of us are not thinking about the technology is when we are asleep, and sometimes even then. Our team members have a background in different fields such as Aerospace Engineering, Computational Science and Engineering, Robotics, and Computer Graphics. Our office is located in the Aerospace Innovation Hub, a start-up hub located on the TU Delft campus in the faculty of Aerospace Engineering.

We work closely with top-tier partners, ranging from government agencies and prime contractors to academic research institutes and other start-ups. Our projects span from large tender orders in collaboration with partners, low TRL research with government agencies, to direct collaboration with military units. Whether through formal R&D programs or rapid prototyping tracks, we operate at the intersection of innovation and deployment.


Your role

You will work in our team of experienced 3D computer graphics engineers, 3D vision engineers, and robotics engineers. You will not just work on some unimportant side project, but you might actually build key parts of solutions that will be used by our customers and partners. At Fiducial, graphics is not just about pretty pictures: our rendering, simulation, and GPU pipelines sit directly at the heart of our perception and autonomy systems. Activities include:

  • Building physically-based and multi-spectral rendering and simulation pipelines (e.g. EO and thermal/IR camera simulation) to generate realistic synthetic imagery and test perception algorithms across environments and conditions

  • Developing real-time 3D visualization and flight-analysis tools for inspecting reconstructed 3D flight paths, live sensor data, multi-camera detections, and point clouds

  • Working on real-time 3D reconstruction and novel rendering representations such as Gaussian splatting and multi-camera / LiDAR point-cloud mapping

  • Building real-time terrain and satellite rendering pipelines that run directly in the loop with our visual positioning and navigation algorithms

  • Writing and optimizing GPU compute and rendering workloads (shaders, CUDA, and low-level graphics APIs) to run efficiently on both desktop and low-cost embedded hardware

What we expect from you

  • Experience with real-time software development such as game, rendering, simulation, or embedded development

  • Solid grasp of 3D computer graphics fundamentals (rendering pipelines, 3D math and transforms, shaders, ray/path tracing, or rasterization)

  • Experience with graphics or GPU compute APIs (such as OpenGL, Vulkan, WebGPU/WGSL, DirectX, or CUDA)

  • Experience with 3D scene representations or reconstruction techniques such as meshes, voxels, point clouds, or Gaussian splatting

  • Experience with modern C++ (experience with Rust is also welcome)

Big plus if you’re strong in 3D computer vision. Because our graphics work is tightly coupled with our perception stack, strong vision fundamentals will let you have an even bigger impact:

  • Familiarity with camera models, projective and epipolar geometry, camera calibration, or PnP, which is useful when matching simulated or rendered views directly to real cameras

  • Experience with 3D reconstruction or mapping pipelines such as COLMAP, photogrammetry, Structure-from-Motion (SfM), SLAM, or visual odometry

  • Interest or experience in applying rendering and GPU compute to vision problems like long-range drone detection, satellite-to-camera matching, or depth estimation

General

  • Full-time availability during the internship period.

  • A willingness to pick up and learn new concepts quickly and to self-acquire missing background knowledge.

  • A high degree of autonomy, determination and grit in making cool tech work.

What can we offer

  • The opportunity to iterate quickly with tight feedback loops, close to the product. We are innovating, learning is to be expected.

  • Responsibility over the things you implement, you are the expert on what you build.

The application procedure

jobs.title: Senior Security Engineer, AI & Application Security
jobs.description:
Senior Security Engineer, AI & Application Security

We are looking for a seasoned Senior Security Engineer, focused on AI & Application Security, to join our Platform team in Amsterdam. Working in a bootstrapped and profitable scaleup, you'll take a proactive, hands-on, senior role securing our agentic AI products, owning an emerging and fast-growing area of security engineering, the risks that come specifically from building with LLMs and autonomous agents, while helping raise the bar on our broader application security practices.

Why DataSnipper?

The hardest AI problems aren't about getting an answer fast. They're about getting one people can trust.

We believe trust is essential to how society works. Every day, we rely on information that's been independently verified, from financial statements to the products we buy, to the sustainability claims companies make. Behind that trust are audit and finance professionals who examine evidence, verify information and hold organizations accountable.

At DataSnipper, we build AI solutions that empower those professionals. By making evidence easier to trace and verify, we help them focus on the judgment and expertise that make their work so important.

For our product and engineering team, this is where things get exciting. In audit, a plausible answer isn't good enough. Every output has to be explainable and traceable back to its source. We've just launched a brand new agentic platform, Alwin by DataSnipper. AI agents running in the cloud across hundreds of documents at once, reasoning across PDF, Word and Excel, with a full audit trail behind every step. There are lots of greenfield problems ahead, and real room to shape what we build and how we build it.

And we build at scale. More than 600,000 professionals across 3,000+ organizations in 175 countries rely on DataSnipper, including Fortune 500 companies, government agencies and all Big Four audit firms. In 2025 alone, the DataSnipper platform delivered more than $1.4 billion in productivity savings to is customers. Backed by a $100 million Series B led by Index Ventures, at a $1 billion valuation, and as proud members of 1% for the Planet, we care about how we grow, not just how fast.

If you want to build AI that professionals trust with work that really matters, this is your chance to help shape the future of audit and finance and do the best work of your career along the way.



What You Will Do

  • Own AI-specific security as a discipline at DataSnipper: identify, assess, and mitigate the risks unique to LLM-based and agentic systems across our products and platform.

  • Translate security policies and risk requirements into concrete technical controls, standards, and guardrails, in partnership with Legal and technical teams.

  • Build a proactive AI security practice grounded in frameworks such as the OWASP Top 10 for LLM Applications, the broader OWASP GenAI Security Project (including agentic security), MITRE ATLAS, and the NIST AI Risk Management Framework, and adapt them to how we build.

  • Threat model our agentic features and pipelines, covering prompt injection, sensitive information disclosure, data and model poisoning, insecure output handling, excessive agency, supply-chain risk, and unsafe tool and API use.

  • Red team our AI systems, probing models, prompts, agents, and integrations for weaknesses before attackers do, and turn findings into concrete fixes and guardrails.

  • Design and help implement guardrails, input/output validation, sandboxing, least-privilege tool access, and monitoring for AI and agent behavior.

  • Embed security into how we build AI, shifting security left through secure-by-design guidance, secure SDLC practices, and design and code reviews for AI features.

  • Partner with product and engineering teams to make secure AI the default, providing patterns, tooling, and guidance rather than after-the-fact gatekeeping.

  • Strengthen our overall security engineering posture alongside the SRE team, contributing to our SOC 2 and compliance efforts (e.g. via Vanta), CI/CD security gates, and the principle that vulnerable code cannot get deployed.

  • Own our vulnerability management process: identify and prioritize vulnerabilities based on risk, drive remediation across engineering and platform teams, track findings to closure, and fix recurring findings at the root.

  • Strengthen identity and access management, secrets management, and encryption across our products and platform, including the credentials and access that agents and AI integrations depend on.

  • Establish detection, logging, and incident response practices for AI-specific threats, and help the team respond when they occur.

  • Stay ahead of a rapidly evolving threat landscape and continuously raise the bar for how we secure AI.

  • Promote secure development practices through developer guidance and trainings, awareness initiatives, and collaboration with engineering teams.

What You Bring

  • Minimum 5 years of experience in security engineering, application security, or a closely related field, with a track record of owning security work end to end in production.

  • Strong grounding in application and cloud security fundamentals: threat modeling, secure design, common vulnerability classes, and secure SDLC practices.

  • Hands-on experience with SAST, DAST, SCA, API Security, Threat Modeling and Vulnerability Management.

  • Hands-on experience with identity and access management, secrets management, and encryption implementations.

  • Demonstrated interest and hands-on experience in AI/LLM security, whether through professional work, research, red teaming, CTFs, or personal projects, and familiarity with frameworks like the OWASP Top 10 for LLM Applications or MITRE ATLAS.

  • Solid understanding of how LLM-based and agentic systems work in practice, including prompts, tool/function calling, retrieval, and agent orchestration, and where they break.

  • Proficiency in a scripting or programming language (Python preferred) to build tooling, automate checks, and prototype mitigations.

  • Experience securing cloud-native systems, ideally on Azure, including CI/CD pipelines (e.g. GitHub) and infrastructure-as-code.

  • A proactive, builder mindset; you prevent problems by shipping guardrails and enabling teams, not just by finding issues.

  • Strong communication skills; able to explain AI-specific risks and tradeoffs to engineers, product managers, and leadership.

  • Entrepreneurial mindset with the ability to thrive in a fast-moving scale-up, set technical direction, influence without authority, and mentor other engineers while defining a practice that doesn't yet have a playbook.

Preferred Qualifications

  • Hands-on experience red teaming or pentesting AI/LLM systems.

  • Familiarity with the OWASP GenAI Security Project's agentic security work and emerging standards for securing autonomous agents.

  • Experience with AI security tooling such as guardrail frameworks, LLM firewalls, prompt-injection scanners, or AI red-teaming tools.

  • Experience implementing security controls in production agentic systems, including sandboxing, least-privilege tool access, and runtime monitoring.

  • Familiarity with compliance frameworks (SOC 2, ISO 27001) and tools like Vanta.

  • Experience with observability and monitoring tooling (e.g. Grafana).

  • Relevant security certifications (e.g. OSCP, GIAC, or AI-security-specific credentials).

  • Experience in fintech, audit technology, or other regulated, trust-sensitive domains.

  • Familiarity with responsible AI, model governance, or AI safety concepts.

What We Offer:

  • Be part of one of the fastest-growing, profitable unicorn scale-ups in the Netherlands with a global impact

  • Equity (Stock Appreciation Rights) to share the company's success and growth

  • Pension plan with a 6% contribution on top of your base salary

  • 28 vacation days per year (full-time) to support your work-life balance

  • Hybrid work model with at least 3 days onsite in our dynamic Amsterdam office

  • Daily, freshly prepared lunches by our in-house chef to keep you energized

  • NS business card for easy commuting to the office if applicable

  • Access to continuous learning and development initiatives to grow your skills

  • Engage with a vibrant international team spread across five global offices

  • Company-wide events like DataSnipper GO, where global teams come together

  • Access to a mental health and wellness platform supporting your wellbeing


Recruitment Process

  • Recruitment Screen (30 minutes, online)

  • Hiring Manager Interview (30 minutes, online)

  • Assessment Interview (60 minutes, on-site)

  • Final Interview (30 minutes, online)


At DataSnipper, we believe great ideas come from different perspectives, experiences, and backgrounds. We are committed to building an inclusive workplace and providing every candidate with a fair and equitable hiring experience.

Our hiring decisions are merit-based and grounded in the skills, experience, potential, and capabilities relevant to the role.

We welcome applicants regardless of age, race, ethnicity, nationality, gender, gender identity or expression, sexual orientation, religion, disability, or any other characteristic that makes you, you.

What matters to us is what you can bring to the role, the team, and DataSnipper. 🚀

jobs.title: Head of Operational Integration
jobs.description:
Head of Operational Integration

About Andercore

Andercore is the AI-native supplier of industrial materials and goods for energy and infrastructure. We execute trade and distribution end-to-end, on our own account, at the speed of compute - and we are becoming the supplier of record for the entire industry.

Industrial procurement is a €900B market in Europe alone and the largest manual market on earth. 95% of customers have no direct access to global supply chains. Materials pass through four or five intermediaries before they reach a site, and 40% of the margin evaporates on the way. For decades, the operating system of this industry was people: people to source, negotiate, finance, ship, and sell.

We built the alternative from scratch. We are the supplier. We buy from global sources and sell to European customers on our own account. Our AI runs the full trade: sourcing, quality, pricing, sales, logistics, credit, and financing. One request. A firm quote in minutes. Delivered on time. For the customer, it feels like buying from their preferred local supplier. No warehouses. No fleet. No inventory risk. Every trade is pre-sold before it is bought.

We are also the credit counterparty. Customers are scored and insured in minutes and get up to 60 days of payment terms priced into the quote itself. The working capital behind every trade is bank-funded, not equity-funded.

Where we are today:

  • Strong triple-digit-million euro turnover run rate, the majority of it from repeat customers

  • Seven European markets live, sourced from suppliers across Asia and beyond

  • 80+ people across Berlin (HQ), London, and Shanghai

  • $90M raised in equity and debt, including our $40M Series B, from Atomico, Project A, Target Global, and Inven Capital - with working capital facilities from UniCredit and KfW

The margin is in the bits. The moat is in the atoms. We are building the supplier of record for industrial materials - and redefining how global trade works in one of the largest and most essential industries on earth.

Acquisitions are our second growth path. We buy established industrial distribution businesses in the EUR 20-40M revenue range, owners and management stay on board, and we connect them to our platform, our procurement, our financing lines and our AI stack. Three deals are live, two are close to signature, and at run rate we intend to close around five per year out of a mapped universe of roughly 200 targets.

Role Overview

You own what happens after signing.

Origination, valuation and deal execution sit with the CEO and our senior M&A advisor. Your mandate starts the day a company becomes part of Andercore and it ends when that company runs better than it did before.

These are analog businesses. Fifteen years old, owner-led, hemdsärmelig, a well-run P&L and almost no technology underneath it. They are profitable, they are growing, and they are at their operational limit. Our hypothesis is that our platform, our purchasing power, our credit facilities and our automation take them past that limit. Your job is to find out on the ground whether that hypothesis holds, in which order, and at what pace - and then to make it happen with the management team, not to them.

We do not arrive as the saviour with the AI magic box. We say so explicitly to every seller, and you will hold that line.

What You Will Own

Holding Management from Day 1

  • Access to accounting and financials from day one, monthly numbers on a fixed close, one reporting framework across all acquired entities.

  • Set the baseline: revenue, margin, working capital, cash, customer and supplier concentration. No opinion without the number behind it.

  • Pick up the commitments made during due diligence and turn them into the operating rhythm of the first 100 days.

  • Run the portfolio as a financial participation first. Both companies are growing. Do not put anything into a skid.

On-the-Ground Diagnosis

  • Spend real time inside the acquired businesses and find out where they actually stand, which is never where they say they stand.

  • Map the connection points: procurement, pricing, inventory, sales productivity, logistics, financing, ERP, reporting.

  • Test our integration theses against reality, quantify the ones that hold, kill the ones that do not, and bring the correction back to the CEO fast.

Value Creation

  • Sequence and land the levers with the management team: central procurement, our credit and working-capital facilities, pricing, sales productivity, customer intelligence, automation of manual back office.

  • Decide with the CEO what gets centralized, what stays entrepreneurial, and what we take from them - the flow runs in both directions, several of these companies do things better than we do.

  • Track every lever against the original investment case in euros.

Owner and Management Relationship

  • Be the peer of a Geschäftsführer who built a EUR 30M business himself. Credibility comes from having done operating work, not from a framework.

  • Be the one who checks whether things are as good as they are described, and who says it out loud when they are not. The CEO stays the partner; you bring the uncomfortable version.

  • Manage expectations in the other direction too: we are not a service provider that solves the acquired company's problems for it.

Playbook and Team

  • Codify integration into a repeatable capability: Day-1 checklist, reporting standard, diagnostic framework, lever library, 100-day plan.

  • Make the fourth acquisition faster than the first, then build and lead the team that runs them in parallel.

Scope Boundaries / What This Role Is Not

  • Not M&A. No origination, no valuation, no LOI, no SPA. That sits with the CEO and our senior M&A advisor.

  • Not a PMO. Nobody here sends a 400-line integration plan with traffic lights to an owner-manager. That gets you thrown out of the room, correctly.

  • Not a consulting engagement. You are measured on the numbers of the acquired companies, not on the quality of the analysis.

  • Not a corporate integration role. These are not hierarchical organizations that execute what the centre decides.

  • Not a process you inherit. There is none yet. You build it.

What We Are Looking For

You are an operator out of a private equity value-creation or portfolio operations team, or a generalist from strategy and transformation with real time spent inside operating companies. Roughly eight to twelve years in.

You bring:

  • At least one integration or post-close situation you personally carried, where you can name the specific knotty problem you solved and why it worked. We will ask for that story in the first interview.

  • Operating substance: you have sat in procurement, pricing, supply chain, finance or sales of a real company, not only next to it.

  • Geländegängigkeit. You are comfortable with an entrepreneur who is highly intelligent, rough around the edges, and holds two cars and a boat inside the company. Nothing about that scenario throws you.

  • People work as roughly half the job. Influence without formal authority, because these managing directors did not sign up to be managed.

  • A strong observer. You read a business and a person quickly and accurately.

  • Fluent German and English. German is not optional; these conversations happen in German.

  • Fluency with modern AI tooling and the instinct to automate your own work. You do not need to be an engineer.

You do not need five PMI programmes on your CV. We would rather you had none than that you learned to fill in lists instead of thinking.

What Success Looks Like

Within your first 12 months:

  • Every acquired entity reports monthly on one framework, on a fixed close, with us having access to accounting.

  • Each acquisition has its integration thesis validated or killed with numbers within 90 days of closing.

  • The acquired businesses keep growing. No customer, supplier or key person lost to the transaction.

  • The first value-creation levers are live and their P&L impact is measurable in euros.

  • A documented playbook exists, and the next integration starts faster than the last.

Over time you own integration and value creation for the whole group at a pace of several acquisitions per year, and build the team that delivers it.

Package

  • Fixed base plus a variable component tied directly to the success of each integration.

  • Virtual equity in Andercore at the current strike, with meaningful upside if we build what we intend to build.

  • Direct work with the Founder & CEO, the M&A advisor, the Board and our investors.

jobs.title: Computational Engineer
jobs.description:
Computational Engineer

WHO WE ARE

Proxima Fusion is Europe’s fastest-growing fusion company and the continent’s best-funded fusion player, as well as the first spin-out from the Max Planck Institute for Plasma Physics (IPP). Backed by over €650M and powered by a growing team across Munich, Zurich, and Oxford, we are developing the hardware and infrastructure needed to deliver the world’s first commercial stellarator fusion power plant.

Our concept advances the most mature fusion technology out there, the Wendelstein 7-X stellarator, through two next-generation machines: Alpha and Stellaris. Our work combines stellarator optimization, advanced computation, machine learning, and high-temperature superconducting magnets to unlock higher-performance designs that were previously out of reach.

Turning these designs into a functioning fusion power plant requires excellence and ownership across every discipline, from physics and engineering to software, manufacturing, law, and business functions.

WHY JOIN PROXIMA FUSION

  • You will get to work on some of the most complex tech challenges to bring abundant, safe, clean energy to the world.

  • You'll get to join and learn from an exceptional selection of accomplished and driven individuals.

  • Do your life’s best work and enjoy the journey.

  • Get to show that big things are possible in Europe when you assemble the best talent.

YOUR IMPACT

We are a special projects team within Proxima’s engineering organisation, using software and computation to fundamentally change how complex machines are designed and built. We take on problems where a small team can deliver a step change in capability, with the goal of getting a stellarator connected to the grid as fast as possible.

As a Computational Engineer, you will bring together mechanical engineering experience and strong software development skills. You will work at the intersection of AI and computational engineering, developing approaches to problems that established tools cannot currently solve.

You will build things yourself: formulate problems, develop algorithms, write software, and test it against real engineering needs. Your experience with hardware will help you see what really moves the needle.

WHAT YOU WILL DO

  • Make new engineering approaches possible. Build CAD-as-code representations, geometry algorithms, and physical models for problems that established tools cannot handle.

  • Enable rapid iteration. Build computational methods to propagate and assess hardware design changes at the speed of software development.

  • Develop agent-driven engineering workflows. Build harnesses and APIs that allow AI to contribute to our mechanical design in radically new ways.

  • Make engineering tools work together. Connect CAD, PDM, and PLM systems with computational workflows so engineers and agents can use information across tool boundaries.

  • Stay at the frontier and help to move it. Follow advances in AI and computational engineering, test promising ideas quickly, and develop new approaches where existing methods fall short.

  • Ship early and iterate fast. Work side by side with fast-paced engineering teams, put working tools into their hands early, and improve them through short feedback cycles on real projects.

WHO YOU ARE

  • Strong Python development skills, demonstrated through substantial engineering tools or computational models.

  • Experience taking mechanical hardware into manufacture, assembly, or test.

  • Depth in mechanical design, analysis, manufacturing, or integration.

  • The ability to reason from first principles and tackle problems without established solutions.

  • Care for software quality, usability, and adoption.

  • Ambition, initiative, and a focus on getting hardware delivered.

  • Understanding of finite element methods, including modelling assumptions, boundary conditions, mesh convergence, and validation.

  • Experience with some of the following: CAD-as-code, PDM/PLM systems, HPC or cloud computing, and AI agents.

INTERVIEW PROCESS

  • Recruiter Interview (30-60 min)

  • Technical Screening (30 min)

  • Technical Panel (3x60 min)

At Proxima Fusion, our mission is bold: making limitless clean energy a reality. To get there, we need a high-performing, diverse team that brings different perspectives, challenges assumptions, and builds together with purpose. We know that diversity of thought and experience leads to better ideas, stronger execution, and a more resilient team. We don’t look at how you identify, what you look like, who you choose to worship or what ethnicity you are. We care about what you can bring to the table.

  • Aufbau und Weiterentwicklung von PMO-Strukturen, die Verantwortlichkeiten und Fortschritte transparent machen

Dein Profil

  • Klare und direkte Kommunikation, gepaart mit der Fähigkeit, auf allen Ebenen souverän und überzeugend aufzutreten

  • Erfahrung im Stakeholder-Management, auch in anspruchsvollen Situationen mit unterschiedlichen Interessen und Prioritäten

  • Analytisches und strategisches Denkvermögen kombiniert mit hohem Umsetzungstempo

  • Technisches Grundverständnis und hohe Affinität zu datengetriebener Arbeit

  • Erfahrung in der parallelen Steuerung mehrerer Projekte unterschiedlicher Komplexität

  • Hohes Verantwortungsbewusstsein und die Fähigkeit, Verbindlichkeit in Projektstrukturen zu verankern

INTESCIA - DATA SCIENTIST (H/F) - Stage MASTER II (6 mois)

DATA SCIENTIST (H/F)

STAGE MASTER II - 6 mois

Rejoignez le Groupe INTESCIA, leader de la Business Intelligence en Europe !

Qui sommes-nous ?
Chez Intescia, nous transformons la donnée en levier de croissance. Leader européen de la Data Intelligence, nous opérons le portefeuille de données et de solutions le plus complet du marché pour aider les entreprises à détecter plus vite les opportunités, mieux comprendre leurs marchés et décider avec impact.

Présents en France, en Espagne, en Italie et en Belgique, nous réalisons plus de 75 M€ de chiffre d'affaires et figurons parmi les 50 plus grands acteurs de l'industrie du logiciel et de la data en France. Au quotidien, des milliers d'entreprises s'appuient sur nos solutions pour accélérer leur business.

Contexte du stage

Les LLMs (Large Language Model) sont des outils efficaces, rapides à prendre en main et généralistes, ce qui en fait un choix technique facile pour une grande partie des projets de traitement du langage naturel. Ils ont supplanté une partie des algorithmes de Data Science plus « classiques ».

Cependant, ils ne sont pas exempts de défauts. Ils sont extrêmement coûteux en énergie, coûteux en eaux, coûteux financièrement et ils nécessitent d’importants investissements (création de Data Centers) pour être mis en place.

Dans une volonté de contrôle des données produites et utilisées par l’entreprise (et plus largement de toutes données privées), il est important de garantir que les données traitées soient protégées, ce que l’usage de certains LLMs ne garantit pas. Nous venons par ailleurs de vivre en France, une série de canicules les plus importantes de ces dernières décennies, avec des records de température dans de nombreuses villes françaises. Il est nécessaire de prendre des actions pour aller vers des technologies plus sobres en énergie.

Par ailleurs, le monde de l’IA connaît une période d’incertitude, avec une course effrénée vers des modèles généralistes de plus en plus gros et de plus en plus gloutons en espace comme en énergie. Dans ce contexte, nous souhaitons nous orienter vers des méthodes plus « frugales ». Nous souhaitons ainsi de préférence adapter de petits modèles à des tâches très précises, qui ont l’avantage d’être plus parcimonieux. Un axe principal du travail sera donc de construire des modèles dont la création sera standardisée, avec un minimum de paramétrage à effectuer, et moins de labellisation manuelle à fournir. Nous souhaitons proposer une méthode qui soit la plus générique possible (voir en appui sur les approches MCP/ADK). Les questions clés sont de déterminer s’il est possible de répertorier, créer et tester des modèles pour nos cas d’usages, et de quantifier le gain énergétique de ces modèles en comparaison avec d’anciennes techniques présentes dans le groupe.

Votre mission :

L’objectif principal du stage est de produire un benchmark et une analyse complète des outils de Data Science proposés par Explore. Ce travail sera complété par une bibliographie des domaines dans lesquels s’inscrivent les solutions proposées.

Enfin, ce stage est prévu pour aboutir à une thèse CIFRE, et l’étudiant.e sera encouragé.e à participer à la rédaction du sujet de thèse.

Des déplacements ponctuels au L3i de La Rochelle seront également prévus.

Les livrables attendus pour ce stage sont :

• Un état de l’art des approches existantes et de l’état des technologies utilisées par Explore

• Un benchmark de ces approches sur des données de l’entreprise

• Une publication scientifique résumant tout ce travail.

 

Ce stage sera rémunéré à hauteur de 1000€ mensuel.

Informations importantes

ð  Ce stage sera suivi d’une thèse CIFRE d’une durée de trois ans, financée par le groupe Intescia ;

ð  Ce stage est co-encadré entre le laboratoire L3i de La Rochelle Université et Explore, filiale du groupe Intescia.

 

Le L3i (Laboratoire Informatique, Image et Interaction) est le laboratoire de recherche en informatique de La Rochelle Université, créé en 1993 et labellisé Équipe de Recherche Technologique. Il rassemble une centaine de membres, dont 32 enseignants-chercheurs, une trentaine de doctorants et 7 personnels permanents de soutien à la recherche, répartis en trois équipes : « Dynamique des systèmes et adaptativité », « Images et contenus », et « Modèles et connaissances ». Il dispose d’une expertise reconnue internationalement autour de l’analyse et de la compréhension de documents, notamment administratifs.

 

Les encadrants du côté laboratoire sont : Antoine Doucet et Mickael Coustaty.

Du côté Explore : Julie Queiros, avec une participation ponctuelle du manager de l’équipe, Steven Hellec.

  

• Les étapes du recrutement seront les suivantes :

  •    1er entretien avec Julie QUEIROS, DATA SCIENTIST chez Explore, accompagnée du personnel encadrant du laboratoire ;

  •    2ème entretien et restitution de cas pratique avec Julie, accompagnée de son N+1 Steven HELLEC, ainsi que des encadrants du laboratoire ;

  •    3ème et dernier entretien avec l’équipe RH, pour tout formaliser.

Le profil que nous recherchons

  •       Étudiant·e de Master 2 dans les domaines suivants : Informatique / Mathématiques Information / Statistiques / Traitement du langage naturel / Data Science. 

  •       Appétence à la recherche 

  •       Connaissances en : Python, SQL, Méthodes de NLP  

  •       Maîtrise de l’anglais 

  •       Qualités de rédaction, d’analyse et d’autonomie appréciées.

Ce que nous vous offrons :

  • Poste basé à Carquefou

  • Type de contrat : Stage 6 mois - Master II

  • Horaires de travail : 09h00 - 17h30

  • Carte tickets restaurants

  • Option de télétravail ou flexibilité pour une meilleure organisation de votre quotidien

  • Un cadre de travail responsabilisant, formateur et propice à l’épanouissement

jobs.title: Software Engineer - Creatives Team
jobs.description:
Software Engineer - Creatives Team

What’s in it for you (to start with):

  • Gross monthly salary ranging from € 3.600 to € 5.700 based on a 40-hour work week. This salary range reflects our career framework. Your final role level will be determined throughout the recruitment process, based on alignment with this framework

  • 8% holiday allowance - 8% of your yearly salary, which is paid together with your May salary

  • Saving for old age - we have a savings scheme for old age, which can accrue up to 5% of your monthly salary, or you can get an additional +2.5% to your monthly base salary.

And many more benefits that you can read about at the bottom of the job description!


Your challenges:

The Creatives team works on and is responsible for our Image Editor and related image-processing features.
You will be working on the backend and sometimes a little bit on the frontend of a complex distributed web application. Our tool provides several different services, written in Haskell, Python, and Rust.

In this position, you will be responsible for the architecture, development, and maintenance of new and old image-related features in our application. An important aspect of our work is scaling our services to the next level, so we can handle another order of magnitude increase in throughput while keeping our app fast and responsive. To give you a sense of scale: a couple hundred millions of images are inspected, transformed and created by our services every day.

  • Plan and shape the future of the Creatives suite of features with our tight-knit team

  • Design, develop, and test new product features

  • Collaborate with and review PRs of other team members

  • Improve the reliability and robustness of our application

  • Work on scalability and performance improvements

  • Collaborate with our other product and platform teams to integrate image-manipulating features with other parts of our tool.

Our Stack includes: Haskell, Python, Rust, PostgreSQL, TypeScript, React, Ansible, Terraform, Prometheus. And we run all of our infrastructure on Google Cloud Platform.

Who are you?

  • You have good programming skills in Haskell (or a similar typed functional language)

  • You are familiar with other programming languages and polyglot programming: we regularly need to make modifications in services written in other languages (especially Python and Rust) as well

  • You have at least 1 year of professional software engineering experience 

  • You have experience in tuning and scaling a big application

  • You have experience with web development, web technologies, and APIs

  • Familiarity with SQL and relational databases, preferably Postgres

  • Good working knowledge of Linux, git, and the command line.

Nice to have:

  • Knowledge of Haskell libraries like warp, conduit, async, servant, aeson, effectful

  • Knowledge of Rust and its ecosystem

  • Prior experience in image processing

  • Some knowledge of TypeScript/React, which we use in our WYSIWYG Image Editor

  • A passion to provide value to customers and figuring out the 'question behind the question'.

Practical requirements:

  • EU citizenship or a valid work permit for the Netherlands; you are preferably already living in the Netherlands

  • Available for at least 32 hours a week, with two days spent at the Utrecht office.

Important note: we understand that studies show women may only apply for roles when they feel they meet 100% of the requirements; therefore, we strongly encourage you to apply even if you don't check every box, as we are looking for passionate individuals with potential and a willingness to grow.


The team:

You will join the Creatives team, consisting of five more Backend engineers, two Frontend engineers, a Product Manager, and a UI/UX designer. 

Who are we?

Channable was founded in 2014 in the heart of Utrecht and is a fast-growing B2B SaaS platform that offers a fully integrated way to market your products online. We empower marketers and online businesses to manage, scale, and optimize their marketing. We are now a strong team of 320+ diverse individuals from more than 40+ nationalities.

Joining Channable means you’re looking for a bit more than just a job. Diverse as we are, we all share our love for growth, helping, taking ownership, and creating an awesome journey together. Feel free to take a further look at who we are here and on our Instagram or LinkedIn! Wanna get to know us even more? Give our Culture Playbook a read.

Why Channable?

At Channable, you’ll find a culture that values openness, craftsmanship, and collaboration. We invest in our people and give them the autonomy to drive meaningful change. You'll work on technical challenges that matter, with colleagues who care deeply about the product and each other.

Want to read more about our development adventures? Then visit our inspiring tech blog: https://tech.channable.com/

And if this makes you enthusiastic, you can also take a look at some of our open-source work at https://github.com/channable to get a feeling of how we work together and what our code looks like.

More benefits: 

  • Annual L&D budget of €1000 to spend on your professional growth.

  • Company-wide performance bonus, up to 10% of your annual salary, determined yearly by our founders based on financial planning and targets.

  • Stock Appreciation Rights: senior employees can financially profit from Channable’s success.

  • 26 vacation days + 2 reload days based on 40 hours, with the possibility of buying up to 5 extra vacation days per year

  • Are you going to become a parent? Enjoy 5 weeks of 100% paid partner leave!

  • Commuting to our office? Choose between an NS Business Card or a €0.25/km travel allowance for alternative transport. 

  • Work from our office in central Utrecht at least 2 days a week, and from home for the rest (we'll provide the gear and a budget for extra supplies). Plus, enjoy flexible working hours with a morning start window between 8:00 AM and 10:00 AM. 

  • We offer a 3-week-long workcation; and an additional 3 weeks if you live as an expat in the Netherlands!

  • Your well-being matters: we offer a discounted Urban Sports Club subscription and anonymous access to OpenUp psychologists and resources.

  • Fresh daily lunch: enjoy fresh meals prepared Monday to Thursday by our in-house Chef (fully catering to vegan, vegetarian, and gluten-free diets). On Fridays, we switch it up by ordering in tasty sandwiches and salads.

  • Additional working conditions include massages, even personal training sessions at our Channagym, video games, an in-office bar, and many more!

  • Channaweek & Channaweekend: connect with your global colleagues at our annual team gathering in Utrecht, and pack your bags for Channaweekend, our annual company-wide getaway. 


How can you introduce yourself to us?

Are you interested? To ensure your application reaches the right team quickly, please submit it in English directly through our careers page by clicking the “Apply” button. Applications submitted via email won’t be considered. We look forward to hearing from you as soon as possible!

Interview steps:

  1. If it's a match, Ioana (Tech Talent Acquisition Partner)  will get in touch with you for an introductory call (25 minutes)

  2. Then you are going to have a tech interview with the team members (1h)

  3. For senior candidates, we schedule a system design as well (1h)

  4. After that, we will schedule a culture and role fit interview with the Creative Team Lead and one more colleague (1h)

When we don’t have enough information, we might ask you to work on a short assignment before your tech interview.
Please note that after the interviews and before the offer stage, we’ll conduct reference checks.


Important note: We know that in the current AI era, it's tempting to use technology to polish your interview performance. While we value your ambition, please do not use AI assistance during the first screening,  so we can get to know the real person behind the resume.

Note: Contact from job agencies and recruiters will not be appreciated. Each recruiter or headhunter who approaches us agrees with a donation of €250 to Make-A-Wish.

At Channable, we strive to create and foster an environment of belonging and collaboration, and we believe in diverse and inclusive teams

[Interim] Senior Analytics Engineer (PowerBI & Databricks)

Job Title: Senior Analytics Engineer
Location: Leiden, Netherlands (Hybrid: 3 days on-site, 2 remote)
Engagement: Full-time, 5 days a week

Contract duration: 3 months + extension

Start date: ASAP (mid-December preferred, early January at the latest)

We're looking for a hands-on Senior Analytics Engineer to join one of our client projects and help deliver practical data solutions on Databricks. You'll work at the intersection of data engineering and application development, building simple web applications that let business users view, enter and correct data. You'll also model the data behind them and support analytics in Power BI. This role suits a builder who is comfortable working with business users and turning their needs into working tools.

What you'll do

  • Build data apps – develop simple web applications for data entry, validation and commenting that read from and write back to the lakehouse, replacing manual Excel/CSV uploads and Microsoft Lists.

  • Model for insight – design data models and lakehouse tables that keep data trusted, sustainable and easy to connect across use cases.

  • Contribute to the ETL life-cycle – build and schedule simple transformation pipelines in Azure Databricks / Spark (SQL and Python), with support from the wider team.

  • Apply DataOps/DevOps best practices – version control, CI/CD and promotion of applications and pipelines across development, test and production environments.

  • Support analytics – create and maintain Power BI reports alongside the business-facing analytics lead.

  • Engage with the business – validate requirements directly with users, and spot when a new request is really a separate use case that should be captured on its own.

  • Collaborate on strategy – work together with the Data & Analytics team to align technical choices with the wider data-platform roadmap.


What you bring

  • Bachelor's degree in Computer Science, Engineering, Information Systems, or equivalent practical experience.

  • 5+ years in data engineering, analytics engineering or data application development.

  • Proven experience building simple web applications that let business users view, enter and correct data stored in a database (e.g. Streamlit, Dash, Flask, Power Apps or similar).

  • Power BI experience.

  • Hands-on experience with Databricks; experience with Databricks Apps or Lakebase is a plus.

  • Solid data modelling skills (dimensional, lakehouse) with strong SQL and Python.

  • Experience with Git and CI/CD pipelines across multiple environments.

  • Comfortable working directly with business stakeholders; able to bridge the gap between technical and non-technical audiences.

If you're ready to make an impact through data and thrive in a fast-paced, collaborative setting — we'd love to hear from you. Apply now!
